messages:
maria: Pushed continuous-batching heuristic change at 03:20 UTC (token_budget_target tuned per-window). After the rollout p95 jumped for short calls and overall throughput dropped ~18% on nv4 pools. Notified because customer-facing latencies spiked.

jake: Which models / shapes are affected? Canary only?

maria: Seeing it on small models (rinna-3b, tiny-open) primarily; shape 8-32 tokens. Canary was 25% traffic -> now rolled to 100% around 03:28.

sophie: Any KV cache metrics? Could be miss amplification.

maria: KV hit rate dropped after rollout. Quick log extract below (from perf summary):

```
time=03:22:11 perf_summary {
  model=rinna-3b
  pool=nv4-48
  p50=23ms p95=142ms p99=260ms (prev p95=68ms)
  throughput_rps=720 -> 590
  batch_formation: avg_wait=12ms -> 48ms
  batch_size: avg=6 -> 4.2
  token_budget_target: shape(<=32)=40 (was 20)
  queue_lengths: high=2 low=16
  kv_cache: hit_rate=0.72 -> 0.38
  kernel_selector: preferred=matmul_v2 for seq<=64, fallback to matmul_v1 when padding>0
}
```

kevin: Hmm. Token budget increase for small shapes should allow larger batches normally. But avg batch_size went down. That smells like queue policy interaction or preemption by long requests.

jake: Could be that token_budget_target bumped per-request but queue policy now prioritizes long seqs, so short requests wait longer and often miss KV because their prefix windows were evicted.

sophie: Also saw kernel_selector.log showing a flip: many seq=32 requests selecting wide kernels configured for contiguous KV cache, but with partial cache misses fallback kernels add overhead (+12ms). Profiler snippet: 

```
# kernel_selector trace sample
seq=32 shape_key=32x1 selected=matmul_v2 reason=pack_estimate
seq=32 actual_padding=64 kernel_switch=true fallback=matmul_v1
gpu_hop_count++
```

maria: Repro plan: 1) rollback heuristic flag to previous values in canary (undeploy 100% -> 25%); 2) enable kernel-selector debug for affected models; 3) capture full kv traces and batch formation logs for 10k requests. Doing step 1 now.

kevin: Also add a staging test that simulates KV miss storm + many tiny requests. We might be seeing a lockstep: increased token_budget -> more aggressive prefix grouping -> longer eviction windows -> bigger cold-set for tiny reqs -> miss cascade.

jake: Action items (short):
- rollback to pre-change token_budget_target (maria)
- collect kernel_selector traces (sophie)
- run staged KV miss repro (kevin)
- add metric: batch_pack_efficiency and short_req_wait_count (jake)

perf-bot: Alerting snapshot attached: p95 spike detected on nv4 pool at 03:24 UTC, correlated with heuristic rollout event id=cb-2026-03-17-312.

maria: Rolling rollback now (canary -> 25%). Will monitor.

infra-bot: Deploy event: rollback to cb-heuristic@v2.1 executed, affected nodes: nv4-48 (canary set -> 25%), timestamp=03:33 UTC.

maria: Early telemetry looks better after rollback: p95 fell from 142ms -> 76ms within 4 minutes. But we'll keep traces capture to understand root cause before re-rolling.

sophie: I'll enable kernel-selector verbose logs for rinna-3b and tiny-open for next 30m and add flame-samples.

kevin: I'll stand up a staging job that replays 50k short requests with KV miss injection to reproduce.

jake: Good. Once we have traces let's check: 1) whether queue priority change caused starvation; 2) whether token_budget_target increases cause more cross-batch prefix eviction; 3) if kernel selector heuristics need tie-breakers based on cache-hit estimate.

maria: Thanks all. If anyone sees a customer incident open up, escalate. Adding @oncall for visibility. :thumbsup:
